mappings.note: Blue versus sooty flame from complete and incomplete combustion. Combustion has no outcome in this frame; C 1.3 competency cited, as for the other flame items.
Product of ethanol with alkaline KMnO4 - the ethanol-to-ethanoic-acid oxidation, LO-8's own content.
Use of vinegar as a food preservative - a use of ethanoic acid; LO-8 is the only code naming it.

Composition of soda lime. It appears here only as the reagent for the decarboxylation in the very next item (sha 0b74b1d80703a81c), so it is mapped with that reaction under C 1.3 rather than to C 1.2 as a 'mixture'. Preparation of alkanes has no outcome.
Completes a decarboxylation equation. Writing the products of a chemical change with symbols and equations is C 1.3 at competency level; no outcome covers alkane preparation.
Completes the ethanol-plus-sodium equation. Mapped on the substance chemistry (LO-8) rather than on C 1.3, the rule used throughout for equations whose reactants are ethanol or ethanoic acid.
Duplicate of sha 87a2f306942d40fb (C2H6O used as a fuel). Identified through ethanol's use as a fuel, so LO-8; mapped identically to its twin.
Gas evolved when sodium is dropped into ethanol - the same ethanol/sodium property, asked for the product this time.
Lather with soft water and scum with hard water. Hard-water behaviour is the ground on which LO-9 distinguishes soaps from detergents, so LO-9 rather than the saponification code LO-8.
Names the reaction in a given equation as esterification - named verbatim in LO-8. Not C 1.3, because the reaction named is one of the two LO-8 singles out.
Why ethanoic acid is called glacial acetic acid - its melting point, i.e. a physical property of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Biodegradability of linear-chain detergents. LO-9 is the only code mentioning detergents, and this is a soap-versus-detergent property.
Fatty acids present in soap. Composition of the soap molecule, whose long chain is what makes cleansing work, so LO-9; the manufacturing items in this family go to LO-8 instead.
Raw materials for soap making (oil, NaOH, salt) - the inputs to saponification, which LO-8 names. Family rule: soap MANUFACTURE goes to LO-8, soap BEHAVIOUR goes to LO-9.

POOR FIT. Additives (perfumes, disinfectants, medicines) in commercial soap. Kept with the manufacture family under LO-8, but nothing chemical is examined and no outcome really covers industrial formulation.
Glycerol as the byproduct of saponification - a product of the reaction LO-8 names explicitly.
Fermentation in the presence of air yields ethanoic acid because the ethanol is oxidised. The oxidation step is LO-8's content, so this fermentation item fits where the enzyme-recall ones do not.
Salting out during soap preparation - a step of the saponification process, so LO-8 under the manufacture/behaviour split.
Identifies the acid in vinegar and its formula - ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Electron dot structures of methane and ethane, both carbon compounds - LO-4 of C 1.3 exactly, and the representation counterpart of the bond-count items under C 1.1-LO-3.
Genuinely two-part: (a) draw the structures of ethanol and ethanoic acid (C 1.3-LO-4); (b) explain the oxidation and name the oxidising agent (C 1.2-LO-8). Both are marked, so both are cited.
Defines a homologous series with an example and three characteristics - LO-4's own content, the extended version of sha 4e9e7a4cd15887c9.
Catenation and tetravalency named as the two reasons for the huge number of carbon compounds - LO-3 restated almost word for word.
Identification puzzle whose three reactions are ethanoic acid with sodium, esterification and the alkaline hydrolysis of the ester. All three are LO-8 content, so one code carries the whole item.
Equations for burning ethanol and for sodium in ethanol. Both are reactions of the named compound, so LO-8; C 1.3 is reserved for reactions whose substances no outcome covers.
